name: Wall Walk to Handstand
description: The wall walk to handstand starts in a push-up position with feet against the wall, then progressively walks the feet up the wall while walking the hands toward the wall, until the body is near-vertical in a wall handstand position. It builds the shoulder endurance, scapular stability, and body awareness required for handstand work, and each repetition is a full shoulder press equivalent in terms of muscular loading.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a push-up position with feet flat against the base of a wall.
execution.setup_instructions: Clear the wall area. The floor directly below should be unobstructed to allow hand walking.
steps: Step 1: Begin in push-up position, feet against the wall.
Step 2: Walk feet up the wall — take small steps.
Step 3: Simultaneously walk hands toward the wall to maintain balance.
Step 4: Continue until the body is as vertical as possible (chest close to the wall).
Step 5: Hold 2 seconds at the top, then walk back down under control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe continuously during the walk. Hold at the top.
common_mistakes: Walking too fast — losing control is dangerous
Not walking hands close enough — the body must be close to vertical for maximum benefit
safety_considerations: Have clear bail-out space on both sides
Beginners should practice with a spotter on the first attempts
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Push-up position to near-vertical handstand against the wall.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Slow controlled walk, 2s hold at top
coaching_cues: Small steps — do not rush the walk
Walk the hands in as the feet go higher
Lock the core — no excessive arch
